newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan may bow to Fed hawks' pressure - article.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan may bow to Fed hawks' pressure - article.

text.p: Federal Reserve insiders said Chairman Alan Greenspan might approve an interest rate hike next week amid pressure from the regional Fed banks, according to a BusinessWeek article.

Greenspan had hoped to avoid shifting rates before the presidential election, but reports that eight of the 12 regional banks had requested a boost in the discount rate make a rate hike at next Tuesday's policy meeting likely, the article in the September 30 issue said.
A 25-basis-point rise in short-term rates "won't affect the economy," the BusinessWeek story quotes one dovish central banker as saying. "And if it's a mistake, we can easily undo it."
Even before the recent pressure from his colleagues, Greenspan may have been ready to "placate the hawks," according to the story.
He worries, for example, that a recent minimum wage hike will boost wage growth already accelerating because of a tight labor market, the story said.

And traditionally dovish Fed governors probably will not try to block a rate hike, the article said. Janet Yellen, Lawrence Lindsey and Laurence Meyer have recently spoken of their concern about wage pressures, it said.
